organizations.What they build: Builds open robots for AI experimentation. Its current site lists Reachy Mini and Microduck, a small learning-oriented biped. Reachy Mini and Reachy 2 are already represented in the pilot and are not duplicated here.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: Pollen public contact via its official website
organizations._relationship_reason: A software-heavy student team could propose an open demo and request a remote technical talk or a hardware demonstration; availability is unknown.

organizations.What they build: Designs and assembles compact robot arms in France, including Ned2 for education and industrial robotic building blocks. Provides programming software, teaching resources and integration support.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: education or partner inquiry on the Niryo site
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask the education team for an arm demonstration and Python/vision workshop; a loan or discount is a proposal, not an existing offer.

organizations.What they build: Distributes programmable robots, sensors and actuators, and builds custom robotics through GR Lab. Its GR100 is an autonomous outdoor security robot; distribution does not imply that it builds the other brands it sells.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official robotics-project contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A practical procurement and integration contact for a small lab; ask for a bill-of-materials review or a component demo before proposing sponsorship.

organizations.What they build: Distributes and integrates Doosan collaborative arms, with application support and training for tasks such as palletizing, assembly and machine tending.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A short industrial-cobot programming session would expose students to safety and integration; request training or a demonstration rather than assuming free hardware.

organizations.What they build: Makes the AGC Autonomy Kit to automate agricultural machines. The official site describes surveying fields, planning missions and making an existing machine autonomous.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Propose a navigation or geofencing seminar and a simulation study; a field partnership needs an agricultural operator.

organizations.What they build: Builds electric autonomous agricultural robots. The official November 2025 relaunch announcement reports a €6.4m financing plan. A June 2026 notice ends sales and manufacturer support for Orio and Jo; do not treat those as currently supported platforms.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for a field-robotics talk or public demo around supported products such as Oz. A student sponsorship request should account for the recent relaunch.

organizations.What they build: Designs Bakus, an electric autonomous straddle robot for vineyards. It carries vineyard tools to automate repetitive work between and around the rows.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A vineyard demonstration or autonomy talk is more realistic than buying a full machine; ask the commercial demo team for an introduction.

organizations.What they build: Combines autonomous mowing robots and human teams to maintain vegetation without herbicides, including difficult industrial and agricultural sites.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A small outdoor navigation study or talk on robot fleet operations could fit software students; access to a real site must be arranged.

organizations.What they build: Builds autonomous robots that remove leaves from tomato plants in greenhouses. The current product is leaf removal, not a claim that commercial tomato picking is solved.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A perception/manipulation seminar and a non-production data project are realistic first requests; greenhouse access and data rights remain unknown.

organizations.What they build: Engineers test benches, special machines and robotics-enabled automation. The opened official site describes R&D-to-integration services; the current corporate relationship with Trektor requires further checking.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for feedback on test procedures and machine integration, especially useful for students with limited mechanical experience.

organizations.What they build: Makes robots and automation for plastic injection molding, including three-, five- and six-axis ranges and sprue pickers. Some six-axis offerings are explicitly co-branded with Stäubli or Yaskawa.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: A factory or demonstration visit and controls speaker would teach industrial reliability; a small student lab should not assume access to a production cell.

organizations.What they build: French robotics activity of the Swiss-headquartered Stäubli group. Supplies industrial robot arms, mobile robotics and automation software; this row concerns the Faverges operation, not a French global headquarters.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Request a French application-engineering talk or a controlled lab demonstration through the local robotics team.

organizations.What they build: Builds adaptive robotic machines combining vision and AI to manipulate objects in changing or uncertain conditions. Applications include sorting, specialized processing and nuclear decommissioning.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask an application engineer to review a student vision-and-grasping demo; a reusable perception benchmark is a more realistic contribution than a production deployment.

organizations.What they build: Builds French autonomous mobile robots for moving bins, carts and materials. Its site describes follow-me operation, autonomous navigation and fleet management.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Propose a navigation/fleet-management talk or supervised demonstration; a reduced-scale simulation project can reproduce logistics constraints.

organizations.What they build: Builds EffiBOT mobile robots and navigation/fleet software for indoor and outdoor material handling. Its site describes co-developed robotic products with Manitou.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form

organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form

organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form

organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for an imaging/robot-control seminar or a simulation-only demonstration using public information.

organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: official contact form

summary: Regional leaders span industrial robotics (Sepro, Stäubli and Siléane), warehouse automation (Exotec), field autonomy around Toulouse, and research hubs such as Bordeaux, Rennes and Lille.

Capital follows deployable automation: Exotec’s historical Series D and AISPRID’s 2025 Series A illustrate logistics and agricultural investment; recent restructuring at Naïo shows commercialization risk.

Demand is concrete in warehouse throughput, repetitive factory handling, vineyard/greenhouse work, inspection and clinician-assisted procedures; these are distinct markets rather than one general humanoid opportunity.
For 42AI, regional clusters and student teams offer the clearest route to mechanics/electronics mentors, while open research tools support ambitious software-first demonstrations.

Start with an open, measurable low-cost manipulation or navigation demo, then approach Pollen/Niryo, regional robotics clusters and research teams for feedback; industrial and medical platforms are primarily learning/partner routes.
